summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for uncontrolled type I diabetes with hyperglycemia and ketonuria, consistent with diabetic ketoacidosis, following a viral illness with high fevers and oral herpes. She had no anion gap and stable vital signs, with normal lipase ruling out acute pancreatitis. Her blood glucose improved with continuation of home insulin therapy. Fevers resolved without identified bacterial source, and flu testing was negative. Chronic abdominal pain was managed with transition to oral Dilaudid, and she tolerated oral intake. Per narcotics agreement, no hospital prescriptions were issued. She was discharged with stable glucose levels, instructions to continue home insulin, and follow-up with her primary care provider for pain and oral lesions.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
